title: New reset-arm grep guard pins a substring that is NOT unique to the reset arm — it already exists in the consent-rejection arm
evidence:
Makefile:274 guard literal: 'document.cookie="rt_landlord_id=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";rtPhId=null'
Dockerfile:133 guard literal: && grep -q -F 'document.cookie="rt_landlord_id=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";rtPhId=null' server/priv/static/index.html

That exact substring occurs TWICE in the generated snippet (verified by grep -oE on Makefile:193):
  1. NEW reset arm (this PR): ...SameSite=Lax";document.cookie="rt_landlord_id=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";rtPhId=null;window.posthog.reset();if(k&&window.pos...
  2. PRE-EXISTING consent-rejection arm: ...else{window.posthog.opt_out_capturing();document.cookie="rt_landlord_id=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";rtPhId=null;}});if(window.posthog){try{posthog.init...
detail: The pinned substring already exists in the pre-PR opt-out arm, so deleting only the new reset-arm line would still pass both guards. The regression guard does not actually guard this change.
recommended_fix: Pin a substring unique to the reset arm in both guards, e.g. include the preceding rt_ph_reset clear: 'rt_ph_reset=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";document.cookie="rt_landlord_id='.
